stem: A school has 720 students, including 180 in Grade 12. A proportional stratified sample of 72 is selected.

A box plot has minimum 18, Q1=32, median=58, Q3=74 and maximum 132.

parts.label: c

questions.title: Sampling and box plots

stem: In triangle ABC, AB=7 cm, BC=9 cm and cos(B)=2/3, where B is acute.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Find sin(B), then the exact area of the triangle.

questions.title: Non-right-angled trigonometry
solution: Cosine rule: AC^2=7^2+9^2-2(7)(9)(2/3)=46, so AC=sqrt(46). Since B is acute, sin(B)=sqrt(1-4/9)=sqrt(5)/3. Area=1/2(7)(9)(sqrt(5)/3)=21sqrt(5)/2 cm^2.

stem: In (1+mx)^8, m>0, the coefficient of x^3 is six times the coefficient of x^2.
questions.title: Binomial expansion
solution: The coefficients are C(8,2)m^2=28m^2 and C(8,3)m^3=56m^3. Hence 56m^3=6(28m^2). Since m>0, m=3.

stem: Positive integers p,r>1 satisfy log_3 p=2+log_3 r and log_r p=2.
questions.title: Simultaneous logarithmic equations
solution: The first equation gives log_3 p=log_3(9r), so p=9r. The second gives p=r^2. Thus r^2=9r; r>1 gives r=9 and p=81.

stem: Let f(x)=5-3/(x+1), x!=-1. A function g satisfies g(f(x))=x.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Rearrange y=f(x) to make x the subject.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Hence find g(x), stating its domain.

questions.title: Inverse functions
solution: y=5-3/(x+1) gives 3/(x+1)=5-y and x=3/(5-y)-1. Therefore g(x)=3/(5-x)-1, with domain x!=5.

parts.label: b
parts.html: The chord through x=1 and x=5 has equation y=mx+c. Find m,c.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Find all p for which f(x)=p has two distinct real roots.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Find all p for which those roots are both positive and distinct.

questions.title: Quadratic functions and parameter ranges
solution: The roots are 1 and 7. The axis is x=4 and f(4)=9, so the vertex is (4,9). The points are (1,0) and (5,8), so m=2,c=-2. Two distinct real roots require p<9. Expanding f=p gives x^2-8x+(7+p)=0. The root sum is 8 and product 7+p; both are positive when 7+p>0. Thus -7<p<9.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Sketch both graphs and label intersections.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Find the total area enclosed between consecutive intersections.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations and enclosed area
solution:
sin(2x)=2sin(x)cos(x), so cos(x)(2sin(x)-1)=0. Thus x=pi/6, pi/2, 5pi/6. The intersections are
(pi/6,sqrt(3)/2), (pi/2,0), (5pi/6,-sqrt(3)/2). On [pi/6,pi/2], f-g>=0 and the area is [-cos(2x)/2-sin x]=1/4. By symmetry the second area is also 1/4, so total area=1/2.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Show h has no point of inflexion for x>0.

questions.title: Exponential calculus
solution: The quotient rule gives h'=e^(2x)(2x-1)/x^2. Since e^(2x)/x^2>0, h increases for x>1/2. At x=1, h=e^2 and h'=e^2, so the normal is y-e^2=-e^(-2)(x-1). Differentiating again gives h''=e^(2x)(4x^2-4x+2)/x^3. The quadratic is 4(x-1/2)^2+1>0 and x^3>0, so h'' never changes sign.
